lesson: A daily Donchian trend system chosen on 2021-23 lost on 2024-25; 20-50% a month is not realistic.

One coin (AVAX) carried a +183% holdout; returns spread over few coins are luck, not edge.
Every scalp (1m-1h) lost after fees, even with 55% wins; 4h EMA pullback was weakly positive at 1-2% risk.

Fast take-profits raise the win rate but lose money; 4h continuation patterns with a 2R target were small but positive on unseen coins with very few trades. x20 leverage cut BTC/ETH trades because liquidation sits about 5% away.

lesson: Scale-outs (half at 1R, or thirds at 1R/2R) lift the swing EMA win rate from ~27% to 37-39% but cut the monthly return by a quarter to a half in 2021-23: C1's profit lives in a few large trends, and selling early removes them. Win rate and profit pull in opposite directions for trend-following.

The IncomeSharks daily dual-Supertrend + OBV filter (S1) improved C1 in 2021-23 (+4.38%/mo vs +4.05% at 5%, DD 26% vs 31%, 10 vs 18 losing months) but failed on seen 2024-01..2026-09: -3.3% at 5% vs C1 +17.8%. A filter that helps in one era can remove the next era's winners; keep C1 unfiltered as the main candidate.

Nebraskangooner-style 30-bar volume breakout with a 2R target (G1) and Supertrend+OBV entries (S2) win 41-42% of trades with small edges; the Cheds 8 EMA pullback (K1) is profitable but lost in 2022. None beats C1 on monthly return. The 'Reference C1 B' check row is recorded twice (once per check run); it is the same run.

lesson: An ADX-adaptive exit on C1 (A2: exit under EMA20 while ADX(14) <= 25, else EMA50) is the first change that improved C1 both in 2021-23 (+5.04%/mo vs +4.05% at 5%, DD 25.7% vs 31.4%) and on seen 2024-01..2026-09 (+18.6% vs +17.8%, DD 22.0% vs 24.3%, 13 vs 17 losing months). Cutting losers faster in weak trends while letting strong trends run adapts better than entry filters.

Entry filters (taker order flow A4, volatility expansion A6) and tighter trailing stops (Chandelier A3) lower drawdown but cut C1's few big winners, so monthly return falls. KAMA trend (A1) is flat; the trend/range switch (A5) lost in 2022 (inferred: the Bollinger reversion leg, since C1 alone was positive that year). A2's edge on 2024-26 is thin and vanishes with costs x2 (+1.5%).

Cross-check 2026-10-19 (two blind rebuilds from a written spec + one code audit, Claude subagents): the engine's C1/A2 numbers reproduce within ~1% when the 5% daily-loss breaker counts realized P&L only (as the engine does, src/risk/circuit_breakers.py); no look-ahead, fee or funding bug found. If the breaker counts mark-to-market losses, returns fall a lot (A2 5% dev +225% vs +488%; 2024-26/09 A2 +14.5% vs C1 +26.6%), so A2's edge over C1 depends on that definition.

Audit facts: after 3 losses risk halves and recovers only after 3 wins in a row, so ~95% of '5%' trades run at 2.5% (and '2%' at 1%); one SOL trade (2023-10-15..11-17) made ~57% of A2 5% dev profit and the top 2 ~78%; the liquidation-buffer gate rejects ~19-20 SOL signals with stops >~19.5% away; max drawdown is on 15m closes (no intrabar lows), so it is understated.

lesson: Gatev-Goetzmann-Rouwenhorst distance pairs on the top-10 perpetuals (one sleeve per coin, net leg sign, 3 daily-ATR stop): the 12-month formation / 6-month trading original (P1) trades rarely (24 trades in 2021-23) and made +0.38% a month at 5% with a 3.8% drawdown; 3-month formation variants (P2/P3) trade 5-7x more and are flat after costs. Faster pairs churn into fees; slow pairs keep the edge.

Frozen P1 (5%, 8b23f23) made +8.6% on seen top-10 2024-01..2026-09 with a 3.7% drawdown, positive each year (+3.9/+0.7/+3.8), +8.3% with costs x2, no trade in 2026-10-01..17. First method positive every seen year with a drawdown < 4%, but tiny and on 34 trades only; return/drawdown 2.3 vs C1 1.3. Market-neutral pairs are a diversifier, not a 10%-a-month engine.
